images.title: Left is smaller on a line
images.purpose: Show that on a number line the number further left is smaller, so −4 < −3.
images.composition: One horizontal number line across the page, centred, with two big marked points and a short comparison line below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal grey #6B7280 number line with 9 equal ticks, evenly spaced, from −4 to +4. Point −4 is a large amber #E69F00 dot, point −3 is a large teal #0072B2 dot, next to each other. Only the ticks at −4, −3 and 0 carry numbers. Below, centred: the line −4 < −3. Exactly 9 ticks, 2 dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a tick count other than 9, or ticks unevenly spaced, or the dot at −4 drawn to the right of the dot at −3
images.takeaway: On the number line, the number further left is smaller.
images.description: A number line from −4 to +4 with an amber dot at −4 left of a teal dot at −3, and −4 < −3 written below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two dots and say which is further left, then read the comparison.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
